formats.name: URDF
formats.contains: Links, joint frames and limits, visual and collision geometry, and inertial properties.
formats.use: Inspect articulation and establish the target skeleton. A robot description alone supplies neither a motion clip nor a trained controller.
formats.status: Interactive previews and complete packages in this archive.

formats.name: MJCF
formats.contains: MuJoCo bodies, joints, geometry, actuators, sensors, contacts and simulation settings.
formats.use: Validate a robot’s motion with dynamics and a controller. Converting a URDF requires checking actuators, collision geometry and physical parameters.
formats.status: Useful next simulation format; no MJCF viewer or simulator on this site yet.

formats.name: USD / USD physics schemas
formats.contains: Composed scene assets, transforms, materials and animation; physics schemas can describe rigid bodies and joints.
formats.use: Assemble robots, objects, sensors and environments for simulation workflows. A plain USD scene need not contain physics or robot action semantics.
formats.status: A future scene export or simulator handoff.

formats.name: glTF / GLB
formats.contains: Meshes, materials, a scene hierarchy, skinning and animation channels. GLB packages glTF assets in a binary container.
formats.use: Show skinned people, animals and animated characters efficiently in a browser. Preserve robot joints, limits and actuator metadata separately.
formats.status: A useful next browser preview format; not currently imported.

formats.name: STL / OBJ / DAE
formats.contains: STL stores a triangle surface; OBJ can reference materials; DAE can also carry scene, skin and animation data.
formats.use: Supply link geometry or interchange assets. An isolated mesh does not establish a robot’s joint graph, limits or motor commands.
formats.status: The current robot previews use STL link meshes. Some packages retain upstream DAE assets.

formats.name: BVH / FBX
formats.contains: BVH stores a skeleton and sampled motion channels. FBX can carry a richer rigged character scene and animation.
formats.use: Bring mocap or authored animation into a retargeting workflow. Read rotation order, units, frame rate and rest pose before transferring motion.
formats.status: Future motion imports; neither is directly playable on this site yet.

formats.name: SMPL-family parameters / NPZ
formats.contains: A model-specific parameter schema may include body shape, joint rotations, root translation and sampled motion. NPZ is an array container, not a universal pose schema.
formats.use: Represent a human motion source for fitting, analysis or retargeting. Match SMPL, SMPL-H or SMPL-X, the parameter ordering and the licensed model implementation.
formats.status: Model-specific pose JSON from the procedural SMPL, SMPL+H, SMPL-X and STAR demonstrators. Sharpa hybrid exports separate body and robot commands. No licensed weights or NPZ importer.

formats.name: rosbag2 / MCAP
formats.contains: Timestamped messages such as camera observations, joint states, transforms and controller commands. MCAP is one storage format used with rosbag2.
formats.use: Record real robot behavior. Recover message schemas, time alignment, calibration and episode boundaries before turning logs into training examples.
formats.status: Useful for a future recording-to-episode workflow.

formats.name: RLDS / LeRobotDataset
formats.contains: Observations, actions and episode metadata. RLDS defines episode/step conventions; LeRobotDataset v3 organizes tabular signals, video and metadata with Parquet, MP4 and JSON.
formats.use: Feed policy training and evaluation with an explicit action schema. HDF5 or Zarr can also store arrays, but a container alone does not define units or controller meaning.
formats.status: Useful future episode exports; no training pipeline runs in this website.

goals.label: Explore all sources
goals.note: Start with the behavior you want to learn, then check embodiment, observations and action labels. These sources are complementary; they are not interchangeable training sets.

goals.label: Humanoid motion and tracking
goals.note: Human motion can supply reference trajectories or motion priors. Retarget to the chosen robot, then validate contacts, joint limits and tracking in simulation before hardware execution.

goals.label: Robot manipulation policies
goals.note: Prioritize demonstrations with robot observations and recorded commands. Match the target’s cameras, gripper, control frame, action mode and frequency; plan to collect target-robot data.

goals.label: Learning from human demonstrations
goals.note: Human pose and video can teach intent, perception and motion structure. They do not provide the target robot’s actions; correspondence, retargeting or additional robot supervision is needed.

datasets.name: AMASS
datasets.contains: Motion-capture collections unified through fitted parametric human body models.
datasets.use: Human motion priors, motion analysis and reference trajectories for humanoid tracking.
datasets.gap: No target-robot actuator commands. Match the body-model version, retarget the motion and validate physical feasibility.
datasets.access: Registration and acceptance of the AMASS research terms. The published licence restricts commercial use and redistribution; model access is separate.

datasets.name: LaFAN1
datasets.contains: BVH human animation sequences and a motion-transition benchmark.
datasets.use: Skeleton playback, motion completion and retargeting experiments.
datasets.gap: No robot observations or motor actions; contact and balance need additional treatment.
datasets.access: The publisher identifies the dataset as CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Check those terms before redistributing clips or converted derivatives.

datasets.name: EgoDex
datasets.contains: Egocentric manipulation video, 3D head, upper-body and hand pose annotations, and language annotations.
datasets.use: Human manipulation understanding and perception or motion representations for learning from people.
datasets.gap: Human tracking annotations are not robot control labels. Map hands, objects and coordinate frames to the target embodiment.
datasets.access: Public download links. The publisher labels the dataset CC BY-NC-ND; its code has separate terms.

datasets.name: DROID
datasets.contains: Real manipulation episodes with camera observations, robot state, actions and task language; RLDS access is documented.
datasets.use: Visual manipulation imitation learning and broader scene coverage.
datasets.gap: Collected on a particular manipulation platform. Inspect action variants, calibration and timing before adapting to a humanoid arm.
datasets.access: The official project documents public dataset access. Follow the dataset release’s terms and schema, separately from the platform code’s licence.

datasets.name: BridgeData V2
datasets.contains: Robot manipulation demonstrations across tasks and environments, with image observations and actions.
datasets.use: Goal- or language-conditioned manipulation and transfer experiments.
datasets.gap: The collecting robot and gripper determine what the actions mean. These episodes do not teach whole-body humanoid balance.
datasets.access: Public download instructions; the project states CC BY 4.0 for the data.

datasets.name: Open X-Embodiment
datasets.contains: A collection of robot datasets with RLDS conversion and loading tools spanning different embodiments.
datasets.use: Pretraining across robots and testing transfer between embodiments.
datasets.gap: A shared episode format does not make every action vector equivalent. Normalize each source’s frames, gripper convention, frequency and action semantics.
datasets.access: Read the dataset list and each contributing dataset’s terms. There is no single blanket data licence implied by the tooling’s licence.

actions.label: One pose
actions.description: A pose is a configuration at one instant. The demonstrator exports 24 local axis-angle rotations in radians, plus root translation. Shape parameters describe proportions, not movement.
actions.caution: A pose has no duration or controller. Euler angles, axis-angle vectors and quaternions must be explicitly identified; they cannot be swapped as raw numbers.

actions.label: Motion over time
actions.description: A clip is a sequence of poses and root transforms with timestamps or a frame rate. Contact labels, when available, help preserve planted feet and object interactions during retargeting.
actions.caution: A visually plausible clip is not proof of robot balance or actuator feasibility. Retargeted references still need a tracking controller and physical validation.

actions.label: Joint-space command
actions.description: A controller may accept desired joint positions, velocities or torques. The action vector follows a named joint order and has an explicit unit and control period.
actions.caution: Position targets, velocity targets and torque commands are different interfaces. The same numeric vector can produce completely different behavior under a different controller.

actions.label: End-effector command
actions.description: Manipulation policies often command a hand or gripper pose, pose change or velocity, together with gripper opening. IK or a task-space controller converts this into joint behavior.
actions.caution: Declare absolute versus delta motion, the reference frame, rotation convention and gripper encoding. A normalized gripper value is not automatically a distance in metres.

actions.label: Demonstration episode
actions.description: An episode aligns observations, commands and outcomes over time. Cameras and joint state are observations; the executed controller command is the action. Task language provides a goal. A learned policy predicts actions from observations and goals.
actions.caution: Record what was commanded as well as what happened. Joint state alone does not reveal the commanded action. Reward, success and termination labels are dataset-specific and may be absent.
